newsitem.title: FRANCE: Six Corsicans probed over island bombings.
newsitem.headline: Six Corsicans probed over island bombings.

text.p: French anti-terrorism magistrates launched a probe into six suspected Corsican guerrillas on Tuesday after a wave of separatist bombings on the French Mediterranean island, judicial sources said.

Four Corsicans were placed in preventive detention and two freed on bail. All were suspected members or sympathisers of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing, which called off a shaky truce in mid-August.

Paris anti-terrorism magistrates Laurence Le Vert and Jean-Francois Ricard placed the six under investigation after a hearing that lasted until about two a.m. (midnight GMT) on Tuesday, the sources said.

Antoine Salasca, 33, Didier Martinetti, 27, Henri Ordioni, 33, and Guy Poggi, 33, were ordered held in custody after the magistrates opened a probe on suspicions of criminal conspiracy, of carrying out bombings and of illegally possessing weapons.

Toussaint Andarelli, 36, a former world kick-boxing champion, and Pierre Confaix, 34, were released after being placed under investigation for criminal conspiracy linked to terrorism and illegal arms possession.
Officials said that arms and ammunition were found in Toussaint's training room.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe has repeatedly pledged to crack down against Corsican guerrillas pushing for greater autonomy from Paris, but few guerrillas have been detained.
Bombings have continued in Corsica despite the round-up of the six suspects last week.
Early on Monday a blast destroyed a garage in Ajaccio, the 30th bomb attack since mid-August, police said. The explosion started a fire which was fuelled by paint stored in the garage.

Salasca, the suspected leader behind more than 20 bomb attacks since August 14, and Martinetti were considered members of the FLNC itself, investigators said. The others were members or sympathisers of the Cuncolta Naziunalista, the political wing of the FLNC.
